questions.question: How many views are required to represent the important details of most aircraft parts?
questions.idealAnswer: One, two or three views are usually enough.

questions.question: What kinds of parts can be represented by one-view drawings?
questions.idealAnswer: Parts with uniform thickness such as shims, plates and gaskets.

questions.question: What is the name for a part of a drawing used to bring out important details and how is it drawn?
questions.idealAnswer: A detailed view, which is usually drawn to a larger scale than the main drawing.

questions.question: What is the purpose of schematic diagrams?
questions.idealAnswer: They are primarily used for troubleshooting systems.

questions.question: Describe an orthographic projection.
questions.idealAnswer: It is a way of drawing an object using different views at right angles to each other, such as a top, front, and side view.

concepts.label: Way drawing object different views right angles top front side view
terms: way drawing object different views right angles top front side view

acceptedTerms: way drawing object different views right angles top front side view

questions.question: Why do manufacturers use symbols on aircraft drawings?
questions.idealAnswer: Symbols are a form of shorthand and are used to convey the characteristics of a component with a minimum of drawing.

concepts.label: Form shorthand convey characteristics component minimum
terms: form shorthand convey characteristics component minimum

conceptGroups.label: Form shorthand convey characteristics component minimum
acceptedTerms: form shorthand convey characteristics component minimum

questions.question: Describe the appearance pf lines used to show hidden views, alternate positions and the middle of symmetrical objects, and give their proper name.
questions.idealAnswer: Hidden views are shown with hidden lines, which are short, evenly spaced dashes. Alternate positions are shown with phantom lines made up of light, alternating long dashes and two short dashes. Center lines, consisting of alternating long and short dashes, show the middle of symmetrical objects.

questions.question: How can you determine if a drawing has been changed?
questions.idealAnswer: A record of the changes is listed either in a revision block or in ruled columns, which may be in a corner of the drawing or next to the title block.

concepts.label: Record changes listed revision block ruled columns corner next title block
terms: record changes listed revision block ruled columns corner next title block

conceptGroups.label: Record changes listed revision block ruled columns corner next title block
acceptedTerms: record changes listed revision block ruled columns corner next title block

questions.question: How are dimensions shown on aircraft drawings, and what is their purpose?
questions.idealAnswer: Dimension lines are usually solid and generally broken at the midpoint for insertion of the measurement. They provide a means to accurately represent the size of an object.

concepts.label: Lines solid broken midpoint insertion measurement
terms: lines solid broken midpoint insertion measurement

conceptGroups.label: Lines solid broken midpoint insertion measurement
acceptedTerms: lines solid broken midpoint insertion measurement

questions.question: What is the difference between an "allowance" and a "tolerance"?
questions.idealAnswer: An allowance is the difference between the nominal dimension and the maximum and minimum permissible sizes. The tolerance is the difference between the extreme permissible dimensions, which may be found by adding the plus and minus allowances.

concepts.label: Nominal dimension maximum minimum permissible sizes
terms: nominal dimension maximum minimum permissible sizes

concepts.label: Extreme permissible dimensions found adding plus minus allowances

acceptedTerms: nominal dimension maximum minimum permissible sizes

conceptGroups.label: Extreme permissible dimensions found adding plus minus allowances
acceptedTerms: extreme permissible dimensions found adding plus minus allowances

questions.question: What is meant by "clearance" when used on aircraft drawings?
questions.idealAnswer: An allowable dimension between two parts.

questions.question: What kinds of information about an aircraft drawing can be found in the title block?
questions.idealAnswer: The part or assembly name, drawing size, scale, date, company name, name or initials of the people responsible for creating or approving the drawing.

questions.question: What information is contained in a "bill of materials"?
questions.idealAnswer: A list of the materials and parts needed to fabricate or assemble the component or system shown in the drawing.

questions.question: What is a sketch for a repair?
questions.idealAnswer: It is a basic drawing that shows specific information and provides minimum detail needed to manufacture a part.
